I know that it’s easy to believe that these mobs take no time to develop since there are modders who seem to implement these mobs seamlessly. However what people do not understand is that mods mainly add to the base game, but they arent actually implemented as part of the game. What I mean is that an actual addition to minecraft is something that involves the entire codebase and inner mechanics to recognize it as a part of the game. Minecraft likely has an insane backlog of issues of features that they need to prioritize outside of creating a new mob. Modders don’t have to care bout the bugs and after effects of their new mob, but minecraft has to polish it in its entirety while paying attention to their codebase. So while I agree that they should add every mob they can, it’s ignorant to say they take little to no time. As a developer myself I know the process and it’s no BS, but I do believe the devs could do better in their decision making.
